newsitem.title: USA: California launches largest air pollution study.
newsitem.headline: California launches largest air pollution study.

text.p: California air regulators launched the state's largest air pollution study ever on Wednesday in the heart of America's smoggiest region.

The $5 million Southern California Ozone Study 1997 will use airplanes, laser beams and weather ballons to learn about ozone, a hazardous mixture of vehicle emissions and sunlight which forms a major component of smog.

Although researchers conducted a similar study 10 years ago in Los Angeles, the 1997 probe will extend beyond the city to cover 80,000 square miles streching from Mexico to the Arizona-Nevada border on California's eastern side.

"Smog remains a serious environmental challenge in the Southern California air basin and its impact on its neighboring states and Mexico," said Peer Rooney, acting secretary of the state Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
He and other top state officials were on hand at a suburban Los Angeles airfield to launch a weather ballon and show one of the six airplanes that will take samples of pollutants from the air.

The study will run from June to October when smog levels are highest and will help form the basis for programs to reduce pollution, including ozone and particles of soot and dirt known as particulate matter (PM).
"We need to take another look at Southern California ozone to fill in gap's in our knowledge," said John Dunlap, chairman of the Air Resources Board (ARB), a department of the EPA.
Ozone has been linked to respiratory problems, premature aging of the lungs, and eye irritations.
Smog has declined in Los Angeles over the last 20 years, with the number of smog alert days falling from 150 in 1970 to seven last year, according to state regulators.
Experts hope the study will help them determine how ozone moves from one region to the other and get a precise breakdown of pollution sources in those areas.
"We're past the day of 'One size fits all' (pollution) measures," Dunlap said. "It's about local district and how we attack the problem together."
Regulators say determining the originate and migration of ozone will help them best determine how to spend money to fight pollution.

Along with funds from ARB and county air regulators, the study will draw on resources from the U.S. Navy, U.S. EPA, an oil and auto research organization and academic organizations from Mexico, Canada and the U.S.
